reviews.text:
Very nice vet
Quite pricey though
Friendly staff
Waiting rooms for both cats and dogs available
Clearly laid-out rooms with clear signs

The fact that our dachshund Liesje could be operated on that very same day, after a severe hernia was discovered, made us very happy. We received a detailed explanation from physician/director Dick van Zuilen. Orthopedic surgeon Roelof Maarschalkerweerd (owner/founder together with Dick) and his team performed this operation with great care. We were allowed to watch this intense procedure through glass, and we could see what was taking place on screens. After the suturing, he gave a thumbs up: successful procedure. All this transparency, including a clear cost breakdown, and the loving attention from their assistants are the reasons for this review. On September 8, 2026, a day after the operation, we received a call from Roelof: "How is Liesje doing?"!!!!

The entire clinic (over 100 staff members) radiates love for animals.
For us, 5 stars. The final check-up today by doctor Kaat Houben was also thorough and loving.
Djedi (2) had an operation to her knee. Very well treated including therapy to help her recovery. Glad we did that.

I had a terrible scare with my dog after surgery done in a different clinic. They were able to help me very fast on a Saturday.
The vets are very kind and polite, they also know what they are doing.
I appreciate that they tell you the emergency consultation fee upfront and even offer to help you find a cheaper option if you can't afford it, truly great and honest.
The best care from Dr. Gabriel Moise! He saved my dog! ❤️🙏

I cannot say enough good things about the team here. We were so desperate when we got here as our cat was super sick. They took such incredible care of our beloved cat and treated  her with so much kindness and patience. The staff is super helpful, knowledgeable, and genuinely compassionate. You can really tell how much they care about animals. I felt completely reassured throughout the entire visit. Yes, super expensive but, still, highly recommend them to any pet parent!

Our dog had eaten a plastic bag and we had to come in immediately. We were able to see the vet quickly, though, and our dog received an injection to induce vomiting. He said give it 10/15 minutes, and if it didn't work, he would need another shot. The dog didn't vomit, and then we waited an hour until he started to vomit again, and he said, "Yeah, it's no use now, and fingers crossed that the dog poops out the bag within 48 hours." We spent 5 minutes with the vet, got one shot, and otherwise just waited for nothing, and are 300 euros poorer with a deathly ill dog. It doesn't feel like they really care about animals, and that it's more about money.

We are very happy that our medium-sized Schnauzer has finally received proper treatment. Anne van Renssen is a star. After being strung along for months by our own vet, she is finally pain-free. We are very happy, and so is our dog.
Clear explanation of what was wrong with my dog. And we also received the test results immediately. And they were super sweet to our dog.

Our young Stafford was critically ill and was admitted to the MCD for 4 days with leptospirosis (Weil's disease). Yes, it is incredibly expensive. But we were helped incredibly well by every single person, from the doctor to the internist to the receptionist. Everyone took the time, took everything seriously, acted skillfully, with care, and effectively, and everything was clearly communicated. They are also happy to think along with you regarding costs and handle it with humanity. He could not have ended up in better hands. We are incredibly grateful to everyone for the good care and that our boy recovered thanks to them. Thank you!
They are some idiots. I waited 4 hours to see my rabbit and no one came to the consultation. And you idiots don't come to this clinic.

Hi team MCD,

Thank you for all the good care before, during, and after our dog Soof's surgery. No matter who you spoke to, you were always helpful and answered all our questions.
My Barbet Beau had a torn cruciate ligament. The team at MCD, particularly veterinarians Kaat and Roelof, helped her exceptionally well. Very professional, friendly, and empathetic. Many thanks!

My dog, who has a life-threatening neck hernia, needs an MRI. Unfortunately, the emergency vet can only help with pain management. I asked how they handle other dogs in life-threatening situations, and the same procedure was indicated. So, if there are no specialists present, your dog will simply die.

We took our dog to the emergency clinic in early September (over a weekend) because she was urinating blood due to bladder stones. She underwent various examinations and was very kindly reassured by veterinarian Kinga.
As her owners, everything was explained to us very expertly and calmly, and we received excellent care. Fortunately, we were able to take our dog home again, and she has since fully recovered.

We thank the team at the emergency clinic
for their excellent care!
Very positive
Had consultation about my dog’s problem; she was checked thoroughly and everything was explained clearly. Overall very professional.

They found a mass that another doctor hadn’t even been able to detect, and they helped our boy return to a functioning state after he had lost so much fluid.

Considering the price point, I only wish the hospital had someone dedicated to helping keep the dogs clean, as this would greatly improve their comfort. However, this does not detract from the excellent care our dog received from the doctors who treated him.
Our cat was terribly bitten by a dog and had to undergo surgery. The explanation, the expertise, the care—it was all excellent. I highly recommend this clinic.
Received good help

Please seek care elsewhere!!! My dog never left this facility alive! We were told my dog would be staying over night for fluids and would follow with MRI the next morning after my dog regained some strength. Instead, only 2 hours after we left the facility they went ahead with the MRI. My dog died of cardiac arrest mid procedure. While my dog likely didn’t have much time left, he died alone on a cold table. The rushed care that my dog received resulted in his death as he was not anywhere close to being stable enough to undergo anesthesia. Now this clinic wants us to pay full price for a procedure not only was he not ready for, but one they didn’t even get to complete because he died midway through. Money of morals!!! Just a horrible experience all the way.

What expertise and humanity!

Nothing but praise for this fantastic clinic and its passionate employees. (from the front desk to the operating room)

We don't like coming back, but if it is necessary, we would prefer to come to you. Thanks on behalf of Maxi (the dog) and his owners!

In the evening, referred to Amsterdam by Anicura; the dog was taken away, but the man wasn't allowed to come along. Then, eventually, one of them came back to tell me that the consultation alone was well over 200. If she had to stay a night, it would go over 2000. Prices far above those of a regular vet. No arrangement, nothing possible. In the end, she was in so much pain, put to sleep. A very unsympathetic and nasty experience. Please look for a vet who still provides this kind of care themselves, like Carlo in Leiden Merenwijk. Super vet.

What an amazing team of doctors, assistants, and receptionists. Everyone was so caring towards our dog. He spent 2 nights here, and the costs are stated in advance.

Special thanks to Doctor Jan; he really put us at ease and provided good explanations from start to finish.

Thanks again everyone and see you soon.

Big hug from Steve the chihuahua <3

I contacted the emergency department early this morning regarding a problem with my dog. I was then guided over the phone on what I could do myself to resolve the situation. Ultimately, this worked out and everything turned out fine. A super sweet lady on the phone; thank you very much for the great support.
Our dog Rico needed cruciate ligament surgery. We received excellent help. They took ample time to explain everything, and we were involved in every step from the very beginning. Very nice people.

Super sweet people, my Bully had surgery for his elbow dysplasia on September 1st. When I entered the recovery room, they had put a nice bandage on him and taken the trouble to decorate it with his name, hearts, and stars.
At the 1st consultation, they listened to me and didn't take any risks when I indicated that I would prefer to have a CT scan of his elbow right away because I already suspected it was an LPC (a broken piece of bone). After the first consultation, everything went quite quickly; I think the surgery took place within 2/3 weeks of the 1st consultation. So happy that they were able to help him so quickly. Now we can calmly start working towards many pain-free walks again ❤️

Lots of love to this team ❤️❤️

Took my cat for an ultrasound on his heart. He’s very anxious so we were nervous he wouldn’t stay still. But the vet and the assistant were so calm and professional, made sure he was at ease and it all went very smoothly. The receptionist was also incredibly friendly and caring. Great experience, thank you 🐱 …

On the advice of our veterinarian, our miniature poodle Cian came to MCD for patella surgery. We found the initial consultation, the day of the surgery, the physiotherapy, and the final consultation to be very pleasant. The transparency regarding the showing of the photos and the explanations gives you, as an owner, a good feeling. Indeed, the 6 weeks of crate rest after the surgery is a bit of a challenge with a playful dog. Yesterday at the final consultation, we could see that it is in good shape. Now we need to start building up walking again over the next 4 weeks.

Great service. Kind and knowledgeable people. They really took the time for the animal, but didn't forget the human and the emotions involved. Yes, the price really could be lower, but that's the case at every veterinary clinic.

Yesterday, we took our cat, who was in terrible condition, to this veterinary clinic with acute symptoms. After the consultation with the vet, we were told that he would have to stay for observation for 24 hours and then be admitted for approximately three more days. The costs would amount to around €6,000. At the same time, it was indicated that there was little chance our cat would survive those first 24 hours.

When the vet indicated that our cat was suffering, we made the difficult decision, with immense sadness, to have him put to sleep.

During our farewell, for which we were given about ten minutes, another vet entered with a form that still needed to be signed regarding payment. After that, we had to pay approximately €700 immediately at the reception desk, even though a large part of the examinations and procedures that had been performed were ultimately no longer necessary for the chosen treatment.

What perhaps touched us the most was the remark that if the money wasn't available, euthanasia was also an option. At such a vulnerable moment, it feels incredibly painful and as if our emotions and situation are being exploited.

After saying goodbye, we were not even offered condolences or a simple "strength" at the reception desk. We stood there filled with immense grief following the loss of our cat, and surely, at such a moment, you expect at least some humanity and compassion.

In short: for us, this was an incredibly painful and disappointing experience. Based on this, we would absolutely not recommend this veterinary clinic.

My dog ​​had to undergo surgery for severe stick trauma. It turned out to be a very serious and tense operation! Fortunately, we received incredibly kind and skilled help before, during, and after the surgery!

All the MCD staff I have been in contact with are friendly, alert, open to conversation, and—not unimportantly—they know exactly what they are doing and what they stand for!
Thank you for taking such a good care of Baloo 🐶♥️ …
They are wonderful people, and yeah, it's expensive, but for emergencies that should not even matter anymore.
Naic

The best veterinary clinic there is. Very experienced vets with a lot of knowledge and very kind to the animals. They take their time and do what is necessary. They think along with you and advise the best!

We received good help. Our dog had eaten chocolate. Sunday evening, 11:30.

Received a shot costing €20 to induce vomiting.

Costs well over €330.
5 years ago, for the same treatment, it was 180 euros.
What a bizarre amount.
A big thank you to the staff of this emergency center. They helped our cat who ate the rope to vomit it. We are really grateful to the veterinarian and ladies at the reception who were really kind.
If you’re reading it - Pixie did vomit the rope, it helped. Thank you so much!
We came urgently for our cat, who had a deep wound in her hind leg. She underwent surgery and received stitches. Thank you for the good care!

Over the past year, I have had to report to the emergency clinic several times with my dog ​​Belle. Each time, we were welcomed at short notice and received very professional care. The last time was because she turned out to be acutely and seriously ill, and on the night before her euthanasia, I wanted to ensure she was not in pain or having trouble breathing. The empathetic way in which they made this possible for us was invaluable.

My cat was hit by a car, broken jaw, one side dislocated as well, eye socket fractured too, no sight left in the right eye. Monitoring Friday night and the weekend alone cost 3200 euros, the entire operation around 5500, plus aftercare. A very good veterinary hospital, but the prices.

+250€ for a 5 mn consultation and to just give a painkiller, exaggerated price, the blond assistant with blue eyes (a little bit overweight) was talking and making long eye contact with my partner in such a way that made us both uncomfortable, on top of that ignoring me completely which was completely disrespectful.

I am incredibly happy and grateful. They helped Storm, my mixed Staffordshire/Bullterier dog, so well. They truly saved his life. Stubborn as he is, he still quickly found a chicken bone outside and ate it; he knows he's not supposed to. But it happens so fast. And this time, things went really wrong. He was stuck in his intestines, a complete blockage, and couldn't pass stool anymore. They truly saved his life. He is already 13 and a half years old, and I thought, 'Soon I'll lose him.' I know that saying goodbye will come someday, but not in this way. I am incredibly grateful to them. Greetings, Renske and Storm. 🐾💖🐾

Unfortunately, it is part of a large multinational and very expensive. But well, shareholders get paid better than doctors these days, though that is actually my only complaint here. Most of the assistants and doctors are super sweet and accommodating (except for 2 terrible ones; one made me and a sick cat wait 70 minutes in a sweltering consulting room after an emergency without sending someone over every now and then with an update; I seriously thought that doctor had forgotten about me...). Standouts here were Dion (?) who gave a really good estimate of the price/treatment and internist Jule M., who is incredibly thoughtful, accommodating, and very communicative (important!) and also sends all reports to your email address. Unfortunately, my cat Muizzie didn't make it after 10 weeks and nearly 7000 euros... but it wasn't my own internist's fault. In short, good and nice professionals, but the prices the big bosses charge people who will spend it anyway because they would do anything for their animal are ridiculous...

My dog ​​Mila received very warm and pleasant treatment. Love and commitment to animals come first at MCD. Despite the major surgery, my dog ​​has recovered well with the help of the warm guidance from the MCD.
If your dog is that sick, this is the medical center to go to.
Good care and clarity. Thank you, ladies.

Our Liv had a fracture in her front paw and needed surgery. What an amazing team! And I would like to make the following observation. It is indeed a lot of money that has to be paid. But I was able to watch everything (from the preparation for the surgery to the surgery itself via screen). And when you see what kind of team is ready to prepare your beloved pet. I counted: about 8 people (including the specialist) are involved. Ventilation is applied, glucose is measured, a nerve block is performed, anesthesia is administered, X-rays are taken, and there is a pre-operative consultation where everything is explained. During the surgery, the anesthesia is monitored, and the specialist and assistant are busy with that. All of this takes place in a very professional operating room equipped with the necessary equipment. After the surgery, another X-ray is taken to check if everything went well, and then she recovers in a heated recovery room. Pain medication is given to take home, along with clear explanations about what to expect after the operation. And all of this with loving care! So yes, a high bill but very explainable and the very best care for our sweet dog! ❤️
Received excellent help with our Carlos, and super sweet people with a heart for animals.

From the preparation to the final check-up... a wonderful clinic, lovely staff, good explanations, and excellent aftercare, even outside opening hours... it's the little things that make all the difference. Worth it just for the artwork on Roos's bandage 🧡

What a lovely place! Upon entering, it is a bit overwhelming due to the size and the number of counters, people, and animals.
Once in the treatment room, there is full attention, time, and love for the animal. You really feel like you are in good hands. After consultation, it was decided that our Vera does not need surgery, for the time being. What great news!

Highly recommended because of the professionalism and love for animals.

We took our dog Max to the vet on the night of Whit Sunday to Whit Monday, 2026.
He had acute neurological abnormalities. He could no longer stand on his hind legs. After an examination by the vet, it was said that he had an equilibrium shock. During that visit, Max's condition continued to worsen, and we pointed this out, but the vet didn't really respond. Max was only given an injection for nausea and to calm him down. However, this did not work. We were sent home, where Max's condition deteriorated. The next day, we went to another emergency vet, who determined that Max had suffered multiple brain infarcts, which meant we had to have Max put to sleep. In our view, MCD made a huge mistake, and the only thing you hear is... sorry that things turned out this way. Yet they make you pay well over €400 for a consultation and a few pills! Naturally, I contacted the MCD for an apology, and you don't even get that. They don't even give you the chance to tell your side of the story. I would definitely not recommend this emergency clinic.
Impeccably taken care of

Hello Team MCD,

We are very satisfied with the explanation, the treatment, and the aftercare Lancelot received before, during, and after the hernia surgery. He is getting better every day and is becoming more and more relaxed now. You deserve a big compliment!

Greetings from Charles and Ingrid and a paw from Lancelot
It will cost you a kidney 😮‍💨, but you do get something in return: expert doctors and good service. …

We arrived late in the evening with our sick Dachshund. We had to wait quite a while, but when we indicated that we felt he was deteriorating, someone came to check on him immediately. We received excellent care and were taken seriously. The cost breakdown was transparent. Because our dog had recently arrived from abroad (now suffering from bloody diarrhea and nausea), no risks were taken. We had to enter through a separate entrance to a special room to prevent contamination of other patients.
Our dog turned out to have ADHD and was saved from death thanks to their excellent care.
We are eternally grateful to them. What skilled, kind, and dedicated doctors.

My dog ​​had a tumor in his lower jaw. What a situation you find yourself in, man. Anxiety and uncertainty, hope and fear. Everything races through your body.

The team there understands that, explains everything calmly, and is always available for questions.
But above all, they all love animals.
A week after his surgery, the surgeon himself called to see how things were going. Consultation is possible, and they are honest.
And now? My dog ​​is clear and has been declared healthy again.
Should it ever be necessary again, I will certainly go back there with my animal.

Very good service!! We came with our dog Isla as an emergency after she had a severe reaction to 3 vaccinations (from another clinic). We called ahead and were helped immediately.

After waiting for a few hours, the veterinarian returned with our dog and explained everything. We are satisfied with the treatment and the service.

Perhaps there could be a little more communication, because at one point we didn't know if it was life-threatening or not, but I understand that they are very busy behind the scenes helping all the animals.

We had an appointment with our own vet on Saturday morning to have our dog put to sleep. Unfortunately, she was in so much pain that we called the emergency department on Friday evening. After being on hold for 50 minutes, they indicated that they were too busy and told us to call another vet in Hoorn. There weren't any available. You don't expect this from an emergency service.

My dog Ivy was brought here by a friend following a tragic accident whilst I was away. Sadly, she was too badly injured for the team to be able to help her, so I can’t comment on any clinical capabilities, but I can absolutely commend every single one of the staff for their compassion, patience and kindness. Thank you for helping me through one of the most difficult periods in my life. ❤️

The emergency department is hard to reach. After 50 minutes, I finally got someone on the phone. My dog ​​was supposed to be put down the next day; he couldn't handle the pain we were calling about. But they were busy. And we were told to just call the vet in Hoorn because that one is also nearby. That one is unreachable too.
Very nice doctors who didn't stress Billie out. Very knowledgeable and clear in their explanations. Took plenty of time for my hob.
Very satisfied with MCD! Knowledgeable, friendly, and well-organized. Glad that our sweet Maine Coon Luna is walking smoothly again after her surgery for her broken hip.
The quality of care is good, but the costs, especially for emergency care, are absurd. Sometimes 3 to 4 times more expensive than at a regular veterinarian.

Our puppy was admitted for 2 nights. He received an IV and had 2 abdominal ultrasounds. Diagnosis still unknown. But we still had to pay 4,100 euros.

Our other dog had a very rare tumor. He was operated on in Utrecht. Surgery with a specialized team, MRI with a specialized team, ultrasound images, and several days of ICU admission with care and medication: 3,500 euros.

Medium care admission MCD: 500 euros per day.
Intensive care admission Utrecht: 111 per day.

Sorry, but the MCD charges insane prices.

I want to thank the veterinarian (unfortunately, in all the emotion, I didn't hear the name) who assisted us so incredibly kindly and calmly last night during the passing of our cat Minoes. It was very intense for us, and we were given all the time we needed to say goodbye. Thank you, thank you, thank you.
Good vet. Unfortunately, very expensive.

Our own vet was not worried about our cat (but we were) and after a call to MCD they indeed told us he needed to be seen. I couldn't be happier that they estimated it correctly, because our cat needed to be hospitalised and the next day his entire bowel system was non-functioning and later they found he had an obstruction. The MCD literally saved his life and we couldn't be more grateful for the amazing care they provided.
Very dedicated staff and a skilled and kind surgeon who took the time to inform me thoroughly and operated on my senior dog Freya well and super fast.
They helped our sick cat very well; they are also very friendly and helpful.

We were referred to Medisch Centrum voor Dieren with our dog for surgery for ED, and I think it is a really great veterinary clinic. They are incredibly nice and helpful, and everything is explained to you well and clearly, which I personally find very pleasant since our dog can be quite boisterous. I would recommend Medisch Centrum voor Dieren to everyone!

Due to an emergency operation that could not take place in Arnhem because of a full schedule, we ended up at MCD. Incredibly dedicated people, including the doctors, assistants, and reception. So much compassion for and attention to the animals and to us as owners. Thank you very much for all the good care and advice. Also on behalf of Pien 🐱

Our 5-month-old puppy had a complex broken toe... we were referred to this clinic by our veterinarian in The Hague.

The staff is so incredibly friendly and skilled... we were allowed to attend the entire surgery... the aftercare was also very good and they are always easily reachable for any telephone consultations... other clinics could learn a lot from this clinic... Thank you for your excellent care on behalf of Leo and us!!

A very skilled orthopedist and very sweet veterinarians, the whole team is fantastic! They support you throughout the entire process. Chase broke his wrist and metatarsals just before Christmas. It was caused by jumping off a cupboard and landing awkwardly. It was completely shattered internally and we were afraid it would have to be amputated. The orthopedist looked at the X-rays and fixed Chase's foot! 4 pins and 6 weeks of tent rest later, and he has been using his foot again for a few days! If anyone deserves a cake, it's the MCD itself! We are so happy again! From the bottom of our hearts, THANK YOU! 🥰🐱 Hugs from Chase and Maike
We took perfect care of our little pet.

My cat recently needed emergency surgery. Naturally, this was an incredibly stressful time for me. Fortunately, the staff were so incredibly friendly, compassionate, and above all, knowledgeable. Without their quick and professional action, things could have ended very badly.

What I also greatly appreciated is that you can always call with questions, and that they are super friendly and considerate. That provided a tremendous amount of peace of mind during a very tense time. I am so incredibly grateful for the amazing care and expertise they provided. Highly recommended for anyone who wants the best for their pet!
Super nice staff, helped me well with my daughter's dog, thank you very much ❤️
They are amazing live safers!! God blasé you!! I do everything for my cat, to make his last days qualitative and pain less.
Great service, and a beautiful end result,

I am very happy with the MCD; they are always available for questions and everyone is very helpful. Thanks to them, the diagnosis of dust allergy could finally be confirmed; otherwise, I would still be at my wit's end, and so would my cat. I am very happy with the immunotherapy treatment and the support I am being offered. Thank you, MCD! 😺

My pup got diagnosed of patella luxation and we were referred to MCD for checkups and surgery. I’m sincerely grateful for all the staff here who helped and cared for her, and I’m sure she feels the same cuz she’s more than enthusiastic to come back every time for her physiotherapy or checkups and greet everyone she meets. On the practical side, the whole process was transparent, the orthopedists gave me clear info and indications, I even got to watch dr. Tijn perform the whole surgery. The surgery went well and the results are good, she has been steadily recovering with the help of physiotherapy performed by Louise and her colleague. She’s walking better and better everyday and building even more confidence😁 a big thanks again!
Good doctors

On March 26, our lives were turned upside down in an instant.

Our 8-month-old dachshund was involved in a severe accident and sustained several serious injuries. Among other things, she had a large abdominal wound that looked terrible.
Thanks to the excellent care of Mike and Jesse, two soft tissue surgeons, her abdomen has healed well, thanks to their knowledge and skills. We are incredibly grateful to them for their good care.

The orthopedics department was also involved in her recovery. They too are skilled and experienced and took care during our dog's recovery, for which we are grateful.

She was admitted to the emergency department where she received adequate initial care. She was hospitalized for the first few days. During these days, she was treated with care in the department.

We are grateful to the clinic for their good, adequate, and skilled care, as a result of which Maeble is now back on the right track.

Thank you🍀

I think it's quite pricey, around 1,500 euros to take in your pet for 24 hours... which makes it easy for people who can't afford to fall into debt. On the other hand, my cat survived. But the costs could certainly drop by half.

We spent a few hours here this past weekend because our 11 year old Viszla was in evident pain and we couldn’t figure a logical cause. From the moment we contacted them through the visit and thankfully good results I cannot but be incredibly impressed and grateful for this clinic and their level of professionalism and no nonsense care.
I am not quickly impressed but this team is simply of the highest caliber 🙏🙏🙏🙏

Our Golden Retriever puppy, Malou, was found to have severe hip dysplasia at just 6 months old. She received fantastic help from the team and Dr. Tijn Wiersema with a 3D hip surgery. Malou is doing very well. We could not have wished for a better outcome. There is plenty of time and attention for explanations and answering all questions. Very dedicated and skilled people. I would recommend this clinic and doctor to everyone!
A 3-year-old dog had hernia surgery and is doing great now. Glad these people exist for animals and the service is very good.

Our dachshund Sjaak received wonderful help from Veterinarian Dick and his team after his acute hernia.
From the very first moment, we felt taken seriously and well guided.

The team is knowledgeable, patient, and meticulous in everything they do.

The hygiene and professionalism were also clearly noticeable and instilled a great deal of confidence.
It was very nice that everything stayed within the pre-agreed budget.
What touched us most was the empathy for both our dog and for us as owners.
They truly understand the impact a hernia has, and we are enormously grateful for that. Dinja, Stef, Dick, and the colleague who spoke English and whose name we couldn't remember for a moment: Thank you!!

Cas (almost 11 years old but very lively) underwent a TPLO operation by MCD Orthopedics (Amber and Roelof) to treat his torn anterior cruciate ligament. Afterwards, he received physiotherapy treatment from Louise. The contact with all the staff was fantastic. They were very caring and knowledgeable towards Cas, and provided us with good information and advice. The operation was very successful, and Cas is walking around happily again. Much appreciation and thanks to all the staff at MDC.

Good care and very friendly, helpful staff. However, the rates they charge are inexplicable. Unfortunately, you have no other choice unless you want to go to the specialist in Utrecht, as they are apparently cheaper. Our cat had broken her hind leg, needed surgery and a pin inserted; total cost 2700 Euros! Our other cat had almost the same thing 8 years ago, was operated on here as well, and back then we only spent "just" 1700 Euros.
On the invoice, they even charged for the blanket she was lying on – €15, whereas you can't get that at Action for less than €5. The follow-up X-ray after 6 weeks looked good and healed. The consultation + X-ray cost another 321 Euros. They wanted us to come back for another X-ray in a few weeks, just to be sure. We cancelled that appointment given the high costs.

Have had several previous dogs here as well? Treated superbly again, both dog and owner. Very involved and treated very well again. Very skilled and clear. Highly recommended. Orthopedics department gets a 10 for everything. A paw from Alpha and a pat on the back from the owners.
In an emergency situation, they gave me the right advice for my cat. Above all, they showed that humanity is more important than financial gain. Thank you very much.

This is the 3rd time my dog ​​has had surgery here. Every time has gone so well, and the recovery with physiotherapy (shock wave and pool) is top-notch. If your pet needs help, this is my number one recommendation!!! Top team here!!! Thank everyone for the great care my dog ​​has taken!!
Hopi, I like it........
They are sweet. All of them. To both dog and owner. With attention and good advice, Lou can carry on without back pain.

The MDC had to operate on my cat Lize. A procedure they perform no more than once a year on average (reattaching the shoulder to the ribs after a suspected collision with a car), according to the MDC. Nevertheless, I had complete confidence in a good outcome, thanks to the calmness and professionalism they exuded. I could call if I had any questions, as Lize had to recover in a crate for 6 weeks. It went very well, and I received a compliment for the good care I had given Lize. I thank the MDC for their dedication, expertise, and also for not incurring unnecessary costs. And everyone is kind and sweet to animals. Thank you very much, everyone, from reception to paramedical staff to orthopedics. Warm regards on behalf of Lize. Mary

Mixed opinion; glad I was able to get the cat there over the weekend, but the diagnosis was completely wrong, and vet number 4 in 3 weeks found the problem in a mere 30 seconds because the inflammation that was already present on Saturday wasn't in the back of the molar, but in the root of the front tooth.
What was clearly obvious to me as a layperson after the vet showed it to me was red and yellow pus.
And I know everyone does their best, but the vet should have found such a clear problem and not sent me home with "make an appointment for an X-ray of the teeth to be sure" and a painkiller, after paying 275 euros.

I am also going to file an official complaint about this with MCD.

They are super expensive, but the care is just so good! Such lovely people, discussing everything and always providing clarity on everything. I was enormously reassured by a sweet text message with a photo of my cat and an update. Thank you so much!

We received excellent help when our Saar had to be admitted urgently. Epilepsy or poisoning... fortunately, she was eventually allowed to go home the very next morning, and it turned out to be some kind of poisoning after all. Everyone was a nice person who treated Saartje patiently and lovingly. Skilled, well-organized, and clear in communication regarding the costs.
Excellent care for our Bram

The most professional and wonderful place.
We recently rescued a shelter stray dog from Georgia. It was two weeks since the arrival in the Netherlands when we went to MCD. We met very welcoming and kind ladies at the reception, and great professionals , young doctors who did full check up on her, xrays, and tests. We also met with a senior doctor, who was such a wonderful professional and person, kept playing with my dog, making sure she was comfortable, getting treats and petting her the whole time we were talking.
We got full details of options, as well as risks and benefits of each solution. Highly recommending this place for anyone who needs it for their pet.

Our 12-year-old male dog was having increasing difficulty defecating. No matter how hard he tried, he usually couldn't manage it and continued to experience the urge to strain. This turned out to be a perineal hernia.

Our veterinarian referred us to the Medical Center for Animals (MCD).
At the MCD, our dog was examined, and the procedure was explained in a friendly and clear manner. Fortunately, the surgery could be scheduled on short notice.

Our dog's recovery went very smoothly! He is his cheerful self again and can defecate properly without problems.

We would like to thank the Surgery team wholeheartedly for their excellent care!

My cat Bub had a sub-operation at the MCD in January due to acute kidney failure. She has been doing well since the surgery! The first few weeks of recovery were tough, of course, but it is absolutely worth it. Glad I get to have many more wonderful years with her. Thank you!

The belly hair is growing back nicely! 😝
Other photos in the tree are from last week.
Very nice people, from the reception desk to the surgeon. After the operation, the surgeon called us the next day to ask if everything was going well with our cat. A huge thumbs up for your clinic ❤️

I very rarely ever leave reviews, but I’m so impressed with this place. I am from the US and have had a varied history of less-than-stellar care from different vet clinics over the years. This place far surpasses virtually all my other experiences. The facility is clean, well-organized, and spacious. The administrative folks are friendly and helpful. Every employee I’ve interacted with has been delightful and attentive. The vets and radiologists and I’ve never been more confident that my dog is in good hands here. It would have been game-changing had we had access to a place like this in the states. The care is expensive, but it’s warranted. If you have to take your pet here, know you and your loved one will be well cared for.

On the recommendation of our puppy trainer, we ended up here a few years ago when our dachshund, just a few months old, broke his leg in two places. We were so incredibly sad because Guus always loved running so much, and we were afraid he wouldn't be able to do that properly anymore. Guus had a pin inserted into his leg at the MCD and has been running like crazy ever since! We are so incredibly happy that we went here and that Guus received such good help. The staff were all incredibly kind too. I can highly recommend this clinic for your loyal four-legged friend if needed.

Because we visited them regarding an allergy, and they repeated everything the vet had already done using homemade medication that was not covered by insurance, and we filed a complaint about this because we felt it was about money rather than animal welfare, and they had also made mistakes with the medication, we were no longer "welcome" with an emergency involving the dog in the evening with internal bleeding. As a result, our dog ultimately passed away because they were the only ones with a surgeon and therefore refused to do anything. It is more of a confirmation that they do not care about the animal's well-being; this clinic is a huge disappointment. Our own vet did what he could in his own time, but unfortunately, it was too late.

My dog ​​Liam had surgery here 2 weeks ago. Before the operation, I had very clear and friendly contact with the surgeon. On the day of the surgery itself, I spoke to him again and he examined Liam. We went over everything very clearly regarding the expectations and the plan.
After the operation, I was called immediately to say that everything had gone well, and called again later before picking him up.
When we picked him up, the aftercare was discussed in detail.
The surgery went perfectly, and I am very satisfied with how things went; I found the contact with Mike to be particularly excellent.

Last Saturday evening, I received excellent help at the MCD with my sweet hamster Dobby. Upon arrival, the assistant immediately saw that something was seriously wrong. An incredibly kind veterinarian was available right away. They were very clear about the options and very sweet to us and Dobby. Ultimately, we decided to have Dobby put to sleep. Sad, but better for Dobby. Thank you very much for the good care, help, and understanding.

Very disappointing experience with the front desk staff – this really needs to improve. 😡

On March 15, I rushed to the clinic with my cat in the evening. At that time, I was actually helped in a very warm and humane way by a friendly, middle-aged blonde front desk employee. She offered me coffee and gingerbread, chatted regularly, and reassured me while I had to wait a long time for transport. That gave me confidence in the clinic.

Unfortunately, my experience on March 16 when picking up was completely different.

I had agreed on a clear time by phone, but upon arrival, I still had to wait at least half an hour, even though I had come by taxi. When I asked for an indication, I had to pay ± €1500 before they were even willing to call the vet. That felt very unreasonable and not very customer-friendly.

They also made a fuss again about the carrier my cat was in. I had already explained the evening before that I normally have two carriers, but gave them to the less fortunate years ago because my cat hadn't needed to go to the vet for 7 years. The veterinarian that evening found the bag safe enough and used it himself. Nevertheless, the next day I had to justify myself again in a nasty and condescending manner.

This could have been handled properly, for example by advising that there is a pet shop nearby where I can buy a carrier, or that I could purchase one at the clinic. If I can withdraw €1,500 for my cat without any discussion, then paying for a carrier is naturally no problem.

What made it even more unpleasant was the attitude of a receptionist with exaggeratedly ugly lip fillers and glasses that looked like sunglasses, who looked arrogant from the moment I walked in, barely made eye contact, and talked about me with a new colleague as if I weren't even there. This kind of behavior does not belong at a professional veterinary clinic. The reception desk is the practice's calling card, and it is important that people who are respectful and customer-oriented work there.

Ironically, the veterinarian herself later did offer a transport carrier that hadn't been used for a while, in a polite and understanding manner. In addition, she clearly indicated that it was perfectly fine to bring my cat in my own bag and left the choice entirely up to me. That confirmed for me that the way the front desk handled this was unnecessary and unpleasant.

Furthermore, I didn't sleep a wink all night due to worry about my cat and even cancelled my job interview to be there for her. Moreover, I am a member of the animal protection society; the lady with the puffy lip filler front desk employee gets paid for her shift, but that is different from being there for animals voluntarily! That is precisely why it hurt me to feel like I was being judged on my appearance (I wear a headscarf and a long dress) and treated as if I don't care about my animal.
Upon leaving, I was ignored again while employees were on their phones. I had to say goodbye myself and received no response.

It is a real shame, because the medical care seemed good and the service at the evening front desk was actually warm and professional. But due to the attitude and communication of the front desk on March 16, I will not be returning here. 😞

Advice to the clinic: choose respectful, empathetic receptionists and communicate clearly. In stressful situations involving a sick pet, this makes a huge difference.

6 stars isn't possible, but they certainly deserve them.
What lovely and knowledgeable people work here.
Even though they are incredibly busy, they take all the time needed to properly educate the owners and answer questions. Great!

Finally, the right diagnosis — we're so glad we went to the MDC
After four months of trying to figure out what was wrong with our Vizsla's leg at our regular vet, we were at our wits' end. Three rounds of antibiotics and surgery later, the infection still wasn't gone. That is, until we decided to go to the MDC.
Veterinarian Hubers immediately made the correct diagnosis. It turned out there had been a persistent infection for a long time that could only be resolved with major surgery: removing the affected tissue and stitching two toes together. A major procedure with a long recovery period, but we're so glad we did it.
What we remember most is the combination of expertise and humanity. We were always well-informed about what to expect, including the costs. The entire team is friendly, helpful, and clearly has a big heart for animals.
Our advice to other pet owners: don't hesitate too long if your own vet can't figure it out. Go to the MDC; we should have done it sooner.

When we bought our puppy from a reputable breeder, we unfortunately soon discovered he had a serious genetic defect. It was something the breeder couldn't do anything about, but it was naturally a huge shock for us. Our local vet referred us to MCD in Amsterdam.

Although it's a one-and-a-half-hour drive each way, it was more than worth it. MCD employs incredibly skilled and honest people, but what perhaps touched us most was how kind and caring everyone is. You walk in with your heart in your throat and your soul under your arm, but you receive such a warm and understanding welcome.

Our sweet puppy underwent surgery at six months old. It was a serious and invasive operation. He will likely never be completely healthy again, but thanks to the care and dedication of the team at MCD, he can now live his best life.

We are incredibly grateful to everyone at MCD in Amsterdam for the fantastic care, honesty, and warmth with which we received assistance.

Kind regards,
Odin and his owners

They're money-grubbing, the healthcare is certainly excellent, but what money-grubbing they are. The rates and invoices they generate are simply absurd. And please pay immediately; it's not stated anywhere on their website. If you really want to experience market forces in all their glory, you should go to these guys. They really love counting money.

My cat fell off the roof, and the neighbors called an animal ambulance. My cat had a broken leg and an injury to the palate.

The cat spent one night at the clinic, had an ultrasound, some consultations, and a few injections.

Cost: €1,500

We weren't even allowed to see our cat when we arrived, and for the actual treatment (amputation or bone surgery), we were asked to fork out another €2,000 or €4,000. At our regular vet, an amputation costs around €1,000.

Why do I feel like my cat was kidnapped and I had to pay a huge ransom to get him back badly injured?

A warm welcome for both dog and owner. Clear information and options are provided.
Extensive knowledge and expertise are available.

Salivary gland removal January 29, 2026!
After a referral from our own vet, Glowy ended up here.
We received a super friendly welcome, and everything was well explained beforehand. The aftercare and aftercare were also excellent.
Well-maintained and clean facilities.
Highly recommended!
Now I can enjoy my owners, my baby, and my boyfriend again. 🐾🐾
Thank you from Glowy.

In November, I suddenly crossed the road.
In doing so, I broke my paw – very miserably.
The result of this unfortunate outing?
Amputation, that was an option, or just an injection.
Fortunately, my owners chose option three.
A visit to the orthopedic department of the MCD.
Dr. Kaat and her colleagues knew what to do.
I now have a beautiful implant in my paw.
My paw is healing well – it's amazing.
As a cat, I'm amazed by such craftsmanship.
My dismissal from MCD was one big celebration.
I even received a present, a lovely stuffed animal.
Ultimately, I'd rather not see you again.
But many thanks and greetings from Mister!

Our whippet needed emergency surgery after perforating himself with a branch. Thanks to the wonderful care at this clinic, he's back to normal after an intensive recovery. He's running and playing freely again! We are incredibly grateful for the expert help.

Last month, we took Daisy to the MCD for the second time for torn cruciate ligaments in her left knee. This also happened two years ago in her right knee, and now again. The first time we went to Amsterdam went so well that we returned for this injury. The care and quality of the staff there are excellent. With lots of love and attention, Daisy's left knee will be completely healed. We are incredibly happy with that. Many thanks and definitely recommended for true animal lovers.
Greetings from Alkmaar

Very friendly, attentive, and careful staff. We went on Friday night at 11 pm because our cat hadn't urinated for a day and a half, and we were very worried it might be something life-threatening, like a urethral obstruction. As soon as we arrived, they gave him a quick check to see if it was an emergency, and the vet told us it wasn't serious, that it was probably a urinary tract infection, and that we could wait until tomorrow to go to our regular vet. We did, and he was treated (if it was indeed a urinary tract infection). I am very grateful for the staff's speed, kindness, and honesty. Thank you so much.

We arrived at 11:45 PM after our dog started exhibiting very strange behavior and signs of pain. We were immediately taken care of by a lovely lady who spoke English. Our dog had calmed down in the meantime, so they asked us to wait to see if things changed. We eventually saw an assistant who reassured us with a quick check of his vital signs and temperature. Since everything was fine, we left without paying anything!

What incredibly kind and skilled people work here❤️
We came in urgently with our Maine Coon and were treated so well.
I was even allowed to accompany them during the ultrasound, etc., and the communication was excellent.
Excellent professional care. Knowledgeable, empathetic, and fast staff. Rates are high.

Of course, we'd rather not come here. But if it's necessary, it feels good. This is the second time we've had a dog operated on here. Once again, the care was so loving and expert. The ability to watch the surgery is also very well organized. The only downside is the incredibly slippery floors. Very difficult with a lame dog. Next time, I'll bring anti-slip socks for the dog.

Regarding the cost, medical care is expensive. When four people spend over four hours caring for my dog, it's understandable that it comes with a hefty price tag.
Pets are expensive, but they are my greatest possession.

Thank you for the excellent care, MCD!

Our 15-year-old dog, Droupie, could no longer defecate due to a hard ring of scar tissue around a large part of her anus, caused by frequent anal gland blockages and infections (after which her anal glands were removed six months ago). The vet referred us to the MCD in Amsterdam, where we were seen quickly. The surgeon was quite confident he could cut away the hardened area and perform an anus reconstruction, and Droupie's age was fine, as she was otherwise fit. The surgery could be performed the same day, and we could pick her up that evening. She defecated that same evening, and she recovered well over the next week. She wears a cap 24 hours a day, and will remain so until the stitches dissolve. We also regularly rinse the area around her anus. The drain that had been inserted was removed after a week. We'll have to send another X-ray in 10 days for a checkup. We are very pleased with the clear communication, the fast and friendly treatment and the involvement of the surgeon and all other MCD staff, and above all, the good work of the surgeon.

On 3/12/2025, we went to MCD with our dog Teusje for a CT scan of the spine. Teusje was showing signs of weakness in her hind legs.

Scan result: herniated disc, and she could be operated on immediately.
What a nerve-wracking situation that was, but I am so happy with all the staff and they were so compassionate. Everything was explained and discussed well throughout, right up until we left to go home.
Teusje is still rehabilitating, but she is doing really well.
I give the MDCD a solid 10!!

Our Norrie arrived at the animal clinic in Amsterdam on December 15th. The warmth and love they showed her were immense. After visiting her every week, February 3rd was her last visit. We received a sweet card and a hug for our Nor; it was truly amazing how much we were cared for there. Our thanks go out to everyone who cared for Norrie.
Friendly people. Good explanation. The clinic looks super neat and clean. A bit pricey, though.
Our Tommy had surgery on his knee 6 weeks ago. Very friendly and skilled people. Everything was explained well and we were allowed to be present for everything. The physio was also great!

Dear MCD,

I hereby lodge a very serious complaint regarding the conduct of the MCD with respect to my dog ​​Angel, a 14-year-old Chihuahua with a tracheal collapse diagnosed by you.

This condition is incurable and was already known to you. You examined Angel for this yourself in the past and prescribed codeine suspension, a medication that demonstrably provides relief from her severe coughing.

Serious negligence,
To my great dismay, you are now refusing to provide this medication again, unless I come for another consultation. This is completely incomprehensible and unacceptable, for the following reasons:

Angel is 14 years old and is no longer suitable for anesthesia
During a previous examination at your practice, she was anesthetized, from which she barely regained consciousness
That same evening, I had to rush her back at 10:00 PM because she was deteriorating severely
She subsequently had to stay in an oxygen tank for 24 hours
This has not only affected me deeply emotionally, but has also cost me a great deal of money
It concerned a known, already established condition for which no cure is possible
Unnecessary suffering

Demanding a new consultation – while:

the diagnosis is established,

the condition is chronic,

and the necessary medication is known and was previously prescribed by you,

is now causing my dog ​​to suffer unnecessarily, because without the codeine suspension she continues to cough and is short of breath. Support from my own veterinarian

My own veterinarian has sent you regarding this:

a written statement (dated 28-01-2026),

and contacted you by telephone,

in which it is clearly indicated that this medication is necessary for her well-being.

My position

I find it incomprehensible and unprofessional that I have to repeatedly ask for medication that:

is medically indicated,

was previously prescribed by you yourself,

and is essential for the quality of life of a vulnerable, elderly dog.

I perceive the refusal of this as negligent, inhumane, and not in the best interest of the animal.

Expectations

I expect:

Immediate provision of the codeine suspension, without an additional consultation

A written response to this complaint

An explanation of why the well-being of my dog ​​appears to have been made subordinate to the procedure

If this is not resolved, I will feel compelled to formally escalate this complaint.

I sincerely hope that you will still prioritize the animal's best interests.

With urgent regards,

Frances
The MCD provided excellent care for my dog, who underwent a total hip replacement. Thank you so much!

We want to thank you—truly all of you. The vets, the technicians, the secretaries, everyone. You have all been patient, attentive, and deeply understanding. The veterinary care my cat received was of a gold standard (and yes, even the bill proudly lived up to that metaphor 😉), but the care for us never fell behind.

The kindness and availability on the phone when we had questions; the regular updates; the time and clarity in your explanations; the way my hairy friend was handled during visits; the participative and attentive presence at the balie; the WhatsApp videos when we could not come to visit; the careful listening and noting of every detail we shared; and the fact that our case was always recognised—never once having to repeat Gatto’s history, because everyone already knew it—all of this was outstanding, both in practice and in human care.

Absolutely unacceptably expensive service for incompetent check!

I spent 1 hour waiting to be told that they have no idea what is wrong with my dog.

Their ridiculous suggestion was to castrate him and if that doesn’t work, AMPUTATE his penis even though, they’ve never seen any similar cases, or could find the root cause.

All that “great advice” for just a 15 minute consultation and JUST €300!

Absolute crooks!
Fantastic help from Dion at the emergency room Saturday evening. She was transparent about the costs and options and very attentive to the overall condition of our 15-year-old Golden. Thanks!
Very satisfied. They listen to both owner and animal and provide excellent care. Doctors with a passion for animals and their expertise.

I have no complaints about the care at MCD. It's great that such good care is available for our pets.

The problem is that the growing demand for good animal care is being used to defraud owners and extort money for exorbitant shareholder profits.

My specific problem, and an example of this, is that I paid €300 at MCD for a completely unnecessary 5-minute consultation...

The exact same consultation had been performed half an hour earlier by my own veterinarian, who urgently referred me due to an intestinal obstruction caused by a foreign body in my dog ​​Dennis. MCD had received all the information from my veterinarian, including an X-ray clearly showing the intestinal obstruction. All of this was reason enough to immediately have an ultrasound and subsequent surgery.

But €3,000 for an ultrasound and surgery isn't enough for MCD. They'll make more money. And so, there will also be a €300 "consultation." A few questions are rushed through (yes, I'd already read that, according to the nurse), the baby's belly is touched a bit, and the temperature isn't taken because that had indeed already been done half an hour ago. Conclusion: an ultrasound, and then the conclusion: surgery.

It's now clear that we have a major problem with animal care in the Netherlands. A large part of it has ended up in the hands of private equity, because they know that people are increasingly willing to pay more for their animals and will pay no matter how much they ask. The company behind MCD, for example? Mars Incorporated, the chocolate bar company, indeed. Their goal? To make as much profit as possible as quickly as possible at the expense of animal lovers.

I'm not complaining about €300 for the ultrasound; two people with specialized equipment spent at least 10 minutes on that. The €2600 for the surgery and medication isn't either; as a layperson, I have no idea what that costs. But €300 for a 5-minute consultation in which literally ZERO new information was gathered is really not right.

How do you justify that as a company? Taking money from people with animals in need in this way?

By the way, you pay €1,000 to stay overnight after surgery. The surgeon's and the nurses' advice was to stay overnight and pick them up in the morning. Had it cost €500? I would have done it in a heartbeat. Going against doctor's advice when it concerns your beloved pet, which has just undergone surgery, is quite a lot. But €1,000? For a night's sleep? Especially considering my previous experience, it all became too much for me.

First, I asked the surgeon what exactly the risk was of taking her home. His answer: "Well, death." A while later, I spoke to the nurse. She started by saying that Dennis wouldn't get antibiotics if I took her, because they would be administered through an IV. But after much persuasion, I convinced her to agree. There weren't really any major risks. I could also administer the painkillers and antibiotics myself, and then Dennis received the last dose through an IV at 10:00 PM, after which I could pick her up.

I went to pick her up, and she was really quite groggy. She'd also caught a nasty cold, with a huge runny nose. I was nervous, but in the end, everything went well. And now, Mrs. is slowly returning to her funny, energetic self :)

Conclusion? It's great that good animal care is being provided! But focus on that, MCD, and less on shamelessly ripping off as much money as possible to make the Mars family rich.

I would like to thank you very kindly for the sweet help I received when I came to you with my dog ​​Diddl; it was the last time for him, but I will not forget it. Furthermore, the card from you was very nice, thank you very much. Diddl's last lick and hug from me provide support even though it is very difficult, but a little warmth helps nonetheless. Thank you. Kind regards, Willie, Diddl's owner. I would have turned 16 on July 1st. But I am glad that you were able to help us when things were no longer possible, because helping is also love, and it is possible. Thank you.

It has now been 2 years since my dog ​​had surgery for a tumor and he is still here 🙏🏼. So grateful for the help, support, and honest advice. Especially the treating doctor Mike Hubers… who came back at night after the surgery because the wound was bleeding heavily. This one is for you. Thank you!!

For the doubters… yes it is expensive, but you won't find more professional medical treatment in the Netherlands. This is a fully equipped hospital …

I want to share my bad experience again because my review has been removed.

On December 7th, I had to have my dog ​​put to sleep due to negligence.

I had an appointment at 9 o'clock and had to wait 2 hours for a blood test result that took 10 minutes.

Based on the results, we were told that my dog ​​was dehydrated and that they gave him little chance of surviving.

The owner admitted to making mistakes because they scheduled an appointment for 9 o'clock when it was actually too busy.

During the long wait, my dog ​​Scooby suffered a hemorrhage.

In a panic, I had to call the reception desk because no one was available.

My son, who was sitting in the waiting room, couldn't reach anyone either; the desk was unmanned.

Eventually, I called MCD on my mobile for help.

Unfortunately, I had to have my dog ​​put to sleep because, according to an employee, he could no longer be saved. I received a small reimbursement for the consultation costs.
This already indicates that she made mistakes, otherwise you wouldn't do that.
It's sort of a buy-off, but this won't get my dog ​​back.
During a phone call with the owner, she told me that while I was waiting, the doctor had helped other clients because they were so busy, and I was just waiting for the blood test.

This made me angry, because if they had acted correctly by putting Scooby on an IV immediately, he probably would have survived.
There was also no sense of compassion during the euthanasia; after 10 minutes we were standing outside with my deceased dog.
He had only just turned 9 on December 5th, way too young for this dog.

Please do not go to this factory; everything there revolves around money and not the animal.
The fact that my post has been deleted says enough.

Expert, caring, honest.
Kick (17 years old) Back on track after a month with a cap. After a serious wound, it required some VERY skilled cutting and stitching by Mike.

Last Sunday, I was here with our cat. His hindquarters were no longer functioning properly, causing him to walk unsteadily. I received good help over the phone on Saturday evening. On Sunday morning, I made an appointment where the cat was examined thoroughly. I was helped very skillfully and with great care. Miraculously, the cat is walking like his old self again.

What a fantastic, skilled, and friendly surgeon Tijn Wiersema. Friendly staff, good physiotherapists, and good aftercare for our little Jack Russell after a major operation. Thank you so much for the great care and a paw from Lusi, our doggy friend.

It’s so difficult to have pets in pain, but the moment we came in, the youngest member of staff saw, acted and showed incredible empathy and care in helping us. A shining example of how care should be administered even under what is clearly a tight and busy operation. Thank you, we didn’t catch your name but will always remember your kindness. Shiro thanks you 🐱
It appears no proper diagnosis was made. It was unclear what was wrong with my dog. Today I went to my own vet, who diagnosed whiplash.

We had our Nola treated here for a TPLO operation; she was guided and cared for very well.
Thank you.
A very nice veterinary clinic where your pet receives good care, but where there is also attention for the owner...

A dog with acute and life-threatening gastric torsion was sent home, and emergency surgery was scheduled for 11–12 hours later. This is negligent, as the surgeon refused to come to the clinic on Saturday evening. Unbelievable!

Our dog Mazzle also had surgery on his cruciate ligament and meniscus at another clinic last year. A long road full of setbacks. A dog who never fully recovered, so the question was... what to do next. Fortunately, we were able to go to the MCD and had a pleasant and honest conversation with Tijn. After the X-rays were taken, we made the decision to have him operated on. We went home feeling very good and full of confidence. On the day of the surgery, we were there when Mazzle was put to sleep. We were even allowed to watch the operation, but we didn't want to. When Mazzle was waking up, we received a call and were able to go to him immediately. We felt such love surrounding us from the staff, because seeing your dog like that really touches you. Every question was answered, and a beautiful bandage was placed on his paw with his name on it. We also received a proper surgery report; fortunately, everything went well, and in this case too, there was damage to the meniscus. The recovery went so differently, and even after several months, I still can't get over it. Mazzle is a happy dog ​​who can enjoy life again. The recovery went as indicated, and we are so happy that everything went so well. We are going to continue enjoying our Mazzle, and he is now happily joining us on our walks again. Mazzle is almost 11 years old, and we are very happy that we still have him and can enjoy him. A huge thank you to Tijn and also to all the staff who took such good care of Mazzle after the surgery! We are super happy with our choice! (and wouldn't mind a tasty photo cake either) :-) Rene and Karin

Our 15-year-old Kooikerhondje recently underwent surgery for a metastatic anal gland tumor at MCD. We initially hesitated about having her operated on at this age, or whether she would be able to handle it. But she was otherwise healthy and the symptoms were too much to continue. Specialist Mike Hubers told us that dogs often recover quickly after this surgery, and nothing could be further from the truth! Just one day after the procedure, she felt cheerful and energetic again.

It's wonderful to see that age doesn't have to be a barrier, and we're incredibly happy to have her healthy with us for a while longer.

We have enormous appreciation for the entire surgical team who cared for our dog with such expertise and dedication. We highly recommend MCD to anyone looking for the very best care for their pet!
Very professional, but also very friendly staff. Clear explanations and attention to people and animals.
Very not helpful vet. Lack of human approach. Procedures over animal care i do not recommend.
Gr of fuk

We went to the emergency clinic after our own vet had closed, and that’s where our dog Mia was diagnosed with pyometra. Lisanne helped us incredibly well. She was kind, calm, and very caring with Mia. She explained everything clearly and guided us through a stressful situation. We’re very grateful for her help and professionalism. Great service!

Totally heartless!! 1 star is still too much. In an acute emergency situation with my dying cat, I was referred to this practice for emergency care by my own vet. However, help was refused with the message 'we are not accepting new clients'. The fact that my cat was in mortal danger didn't interest the inhumane person on the phone at all. I indicated that my cat was dying. What are you supposed to do then??? I couldn't just wring her neck myself, could I?

Ultimately, my 17-year-old cat, in mortal danger, had to travel an unnecessary 40 minutes further to a clinic in Heerhugowaard that *did* provide immediate help. It is incomprehensible and unacceptable that a practice offers no help in a life-threatening situation. I would have so loved to have given my beloved a different ending.

Update Nov 16.
Response to my cat's unnecessarily long death struggle: Too bad... it is too bad when the peanut butter runs out. Not when you are refused in an emergency by the substitute for your own vet. By the way, €11 in call charges on my phone bill for this worthless phone call.

Recently, I ended up at the orthopedics department of the Medical Center for Animals with Sepp the Siberian cat following diagnoses from my current veterinarian whom I didn't entirely trust.

After just one visit to the orthopedist, it immediately became clear that my feeling was correct and that Sepp didn't have hip dysplasia at all, but a torn cruciate ligament.
What is incredibly nice is that they take all the time needed, perform extensive examinations, discuss everything thoroughly, and explain it clearly. Unfortunately, crate rest ultimately proved insufficient, and surgery was necessary.

The staff here are also incredibly nice, and it is very pleasant that you are allowed to come along. Here too, they took all the time for you, and everything was explained and discussed. Clear written information was also provided, and I could always ask questions. These were answered quickly.

In short, a very nice medical center where they are still genuinely involved and truly have all the time and attention for both people and animals.

My previous experiences in internal medicine and ophthalmology have also been very positive.
Friendly and expert staff, and a quick and accurate diagnosis and treatment plan.

Our sweet cat Evy was hit by a car; her head was badly battered. After an uncertain night at the MCD, she underwent surgery performed by Roelof and Anne from Orthopedics. What amazing doctors, with excellent communication regarding the treatment plan. In addition to treating our Evy well, we certainly didn't incur any unnecessary costs. The assistants were also very helpful, kind, and certainly highly skilled; we received a good explanation regarding medication and pain management. Even at the follow-up appointments, we were immediately recognized when checking in at the reception desk, which is definitely a personal touch instead of just being a number. Now Evy has been discharged, and we look forward to a bright future.

Thank you Anne, Roelof, and all the lovely assistants. A big hug from Evy.
We received wonderful help. Lovely doctors who treat your pet with care.

We were received and helped in a pleasant and excellent manner when our Cavalier broke her leg and needed surgery. The staff is lovely and you are treated with care, so a big thumbs up and thank you for all the good care.
Great and professional place! Everyone is so friendly. My dog Bowie had a knee operation and we had amazing assistance throughout the entire process.
The place where your dog is seen. Good guidance, care, and aftercare!
CT scan for my cat in Heerhugowaard 850 euros, CT scan with consultation at your place 1600 euros, 1 word... scandalous

My partner took my dog there as her back limps were found paralysed when he got home from work one day so he took her to this vet hospital immediately. The vet on duty had a quick check up on her and soon after she jumped to a conclusion that it’s best to put her to sleep as she thinks she is suffering a lot! I was away at the time so they called me on the phone and told me about the news. When the vet told me that my dogs is coughing a lot, she is in a lot of pain, she is screaming and she is old so I should really consider letting her go, it just all didn’t make a lot of sense to me as she was brought in for the numb back legs rather than her coughing issue which is an known issue and it’s been monitored and controlled fairly well by the medication already. It was not the reason why we brought the dog in to the hospital for. My dog was not screaming when she was at home and she only started screaming when the vet did something to her legs. My dog has always been extra nervous when she is at the vet so she always pants a lot more than usual. I didn’t trust the vet’s advice and told her to simply give her a pain killer and we would take her home to monitor. I ended up taking the next flight home next day.
Long story short, it turned out my dog simply had a slip at home as her paws are now very dry due to her age and she had lost the grip to the floor. Her legs just went numb for a short period of time as she couldn’t get herself back up for a number of hours. She was able to walk like normal again next morning and like nothing had happened before! She was chasing ball, eating well, and all happy again. I now simply apply some paw ointment to improve her grip and problem has been solved.
It makes me so angry that the vet would jumped to such an irreversible decision without doing a full diagnosis on her and I could have lost my beloved dog! I am fully aware that my dog is old but I’m ready to let go when I know she is truly suffering too much.
It’s deeply concerning to me that the vet had not done the full due diligence in this case and nearly costed my dog’s life! It’s completely irresponsible and they are still denying any wrong doing from their end. I don’t believe my dog had “miraculously” revived herself as the vet hospital suggested because she became all normal again the very next morning, but it was a clear misdiagnosis from the vet on duty!
Not only we had incurred additional financial losses from this, it had also caused us a tremendous emotional distress. I don’t know how many other poor dogs had been mistreated and lathe pet owner had lost their beloved dogs from the similar situation! I hope they would somehow hold the accountability for their action!
Be extremely careful and try to get a second opinion if you have any doubt of what the vet says to you! Especially this vet!

Sadly, my cat passed away there, totally unexpectedly, but in a very good, beautiful, and peaceful way. What was incredibly nice was that the staff were super thoughtful, understanding, sweet, compassionate, and kind!!

Update: Our dog Snoopy was under treatment at MCD Internal Medicine and Dermatology for years. He was given new medication, but suddenly became very ill, with vomiting and bloody diarrhea. On a Sunday, we called the MCD Emergency Post requesting help for Snoopy, but we were refused.

On Monday, MCD Internal Medicine advised stopping the new medication, and we were sent away again to continue treatment with the regular veterinarian. I begged MCD to help him, because I knew the regular veterinarian was incapable of treating something so complex, and I shared this with MCD as well. Unfortunately, they refused again.

Four days later, after yet another incorrect diagnosis and incorrect treatment by a regular veterinarian, my little dog was so battered and had suffered so much that we had to have him put to sleep. He had been a regular patient at MCD for more than 14 years, and we paid thousands of euros, but that was not enough to help him at the very end, precisely when it was needed most! Only after 4 days and my repeated request was I finally called back by the internist (who was acting as a locum and had recently become his treating physician), on the day Snoopy was put to sleep. She offered to treat him while he was dying, at the estimated price of 2,000 euros for the first two days, with extra costs for ultrasounds and other examinations, plus another 700-800 euros per day thereafter. A few days earlier, we would have been willing to pay that and even more, when he could still have been saved!

We are inconsolable and deeply disappointed in MCD.

For the 2nd time, surgery at MCD with Dexter, who suffers from LPC. Just like last time, we received excellent help again. A huge thank you to everyone who helped, and a huge thank you for all the good information and care. He can really whine and talk a lot, but luckily not everyone is as impressed by the noise he can make anymore. Thanks for all the good care, see you in 6 weeks for the check-up. Thanks and a paw from Dexter 😀 Update: after returning for the check-up, Super positive, a huge thank you for the right decision being made for Dexter, building up the final stretch and we are very grateful to you McD for the good care!!!!!
Our dachshund Novi received excellent help. They provide clear information and explanations and give good advice, but they also take into account what the person themselves thinks and wants.

Internist and surgeon at MCD saved our boy ‘s life.

Our boy had a big surgery to remove tumor in pancreas. Doctor Mike was responsible for the surgery. We almost couldn’t see the stitches…excellently done. And internist Dr Celine had extremely professional care for our boy prior and after the surgery .

A huge thanks to them .

Very friendly reception desk, skilled professionals. They work well on time. Our cat Freek was in capable hands there after breaking his thighbone in a collision with a car. Plenty of parking space and easily accessible.
Only spoke on the phone, but was spoken to in a super sweet and helpful manner, so nothing but good things to say about that.

After an incorrect diagnosis by the Anicura vet in Hillegom, we ended up here with our dog. What a skilled and loving team! In a short time, they managed to make the correct diagnosis, and after a day and a night stay, our dog was practically back to normal.
A few hours after we had to leave Larry with them for treatment, we received a sweet and reassuring message with a photo and an update; that was very nice! Thank you for the fantastic and loving care for Larry!

We were referred to the MCD by the local veterinarian for surgery on our cat's hock. The recommendation was to have a strap fitted. Ultimately, this surgery proved unsuccessful. Not surprising, given the process we went through.

Immediate result: 2/5 stars. The paw was misaligned from day 1 (see the attached photo), and the fentanyl (pain relief) patch was applied so poorly that it kept falling out of his onesie.

Aftercare: 3.5/5 stars: The doctors and assistants were extremely nice people. However, even they had the greatest difficulty bandaging the paw in such a way that it wouldn't become misaligned.

Price/quality ratio: 1/5 stars. The MCD is not cheap. It is a big money-making machine. Before the surgery, we were reminded three times that we needed to have the money ready. After it became clear after 6 weeks that the surgery had failed, the option was offered quite quickly for a new, more expensive operation or an amputation. The amputation would cost 2,000 more than at the local vet. Do the operating ‘specialists’ need 2,000 euros more than the local vet for the same treatment? That is an absurd difference.

Furthermore, we have never been able to find out why things went wrong, and as of the time of writing this review, they have already been trying to share the final report with us for ten days. They are, as we were told, “checking for spelling errors.” You don't need two weeks for that.
